short: Attila crossed the Alps into Italy, sacked Aquileia and advanced on Rome before turning back unopposed.
full:
In 452 CE, having been checked in Gaul the previous year, Attila led the Huns across the Alps into northern Italy. His forces besieged Aquileia for some three months before finally storming and razing it so thoroughly that, according to tradition, its exact site was later disputed; Milan and other cities of the Po valley were plundered in turn, and Emperor Valentinian III fled Ravenna for the safety of Rome.

With Italy short of grain after a poor harvest and Attila's own army reportedly weakened by disease, an embassy including Pope Leo I met Attila near the Mincio river and persuaded him to withdraw without attacking Rome itself. Roman tradition credited Leo's intervention directly, though shortage of supplies and news of an eastern Roman campaign against the Huns' homeland were likely as decisive. Attila died the following year, and the Hunnic empire fragmented soon after.
